lesson.title: Real or fake?
lesson.subtitle: AI fakes, and the habit that keeps you safe

video.title: Real or fake?
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (main character)
Mr Okafor — Grade 8 science teacher, Nigeria, the student's teacher (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, talking to the student)

scenes.visual: Cards: A voice message; “Send money now!”; He was right there.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: My sister got a voice message that sounded just like her son. “Mum, I lost my phone, send me money now!” But her son was sitting right next to her! The voice was made by AI.

scenes.visual: The title card: the course, the lesson title and subtitle, the Darsi mark.
scenes.animation: Mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: how AI can make fakes that look and sound real, and how you stay safe.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: AI can make pictures of things that never happened. It can copy a person's voice from a short recording. And it can write messages with perfect spelling.

scenes.visual: Numbered steps: Stop; Think; Ask a grown-up.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: So looking hard isn't always enough. Fakes get better every year. What works is a habit: stop, think, ask.

scenes.visual: A list: Stop: don't click or reply; Think: who? Is it rushing me?; Ask a grown-up you trust.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Stop: don't click, reply or send anything yet. Think: who sent it, and is it rushing me? Ask: show a grown-up you trust.

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A message says: “You won a new phone! Click fast, it ends in ten minutes!” What's the first thing you do?

scenes.visual: A list: Don't click; A rush stops you thinking; A prize you never entered for.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Stop: don't click. A rush is a trick to stop you thinking. And a prize you never entered for is a warning sign.

scenes.visual: Cards joined by arrows: Pick a word together; A scary call; Ask for the word; A fake won't know it.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Here's a great idea for voices. Choose a secret code word with your family. If someone calls with a scary story, ask for the code word. A fake voice won't know it!

scenes.visual: A list: Not even as a joke; Fakes can hurt; Don't share it; Tell a grown-up.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: And never make a fake of a real person, even as a joke. A fake picture can hurt someone badly. If you see one of someone you know, don't share it: tell a grown-up.

scenes.visual: Cards: Eight messages; Real?; Scam?; See the signs.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: In the app, eight messages arrive on a phone. Some are real, and some are scams. Decide for each one, then see the warning signs!

scenes.visual: The quick check: the question and its answer cards, with the speaker beside them.
scenes.animation: The speaker slides in; answer cards drop in.
scenes.narration: Your turn. You see a funny picture of your teacher doing something silly. It might be made by AI. What do you do?

scenes.visual: The summary: Fakes look and sound real; Stop, think, ask; A family code word. Takeaway: When in doubt, stop and ask a grown-up.
scenes.animation: Points tick in as they are said; the takeaway slides up.
scenes.on_screen_text: Fakes · Stop, think, ask · Code word
scenes.narration: Don't share it, and tell a grown-up. Remember: AI can make fakes that look and sound real. Stop, think, ask. And a family code word beats a fake voice.

scenes.visual: A list: Choose a word at home; Not on a phone; Practise the scary call.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it tomorrow: choose a secret code word with your family at home. Don't write it on a phone. Then practise: if someone calls with a scary story, what do you ask?

checkpoints.prompt: A message says you won a new phone and must click fast. What's the first thing you do?

options.text: Send it to all my friends

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Right! Rushing you is a trick. Stop first.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. “Click fast” is the trick. Stop first, then ask a grown-up.

checkpoints.prompt: You see a funny picture of your teacher doing something silly. It might be made by AI. What do you do?

options.text: Share it with the class group
Don't share it, and tell a grown-up

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Yes! Fakes of real people can hurt. Don't share it.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite. A fake picture can hurt your teacher. Don't share it; tell a grown-up.
